explanation: Brute-force login tracking via fail2ban. getbannedip.sh parses 'fail2ban-client status sshd' and writes the result toward banned_ip.xml. Unlike most other entries in this corpus, the detection mechanism here isn't a tag value at all -- it's whether the file has any content. This is confirmed by cross-referencing scanning-lin.py's own logic, which checks this exact file via is_file_empty_or_non_existent(): a missing or empty file means no bans are currently recorded (clean), and any content at all means fail2ban has actively banned at least one IP for repeated failed logins.

known_patterns.meaning: At least one IP is currently banned by fail2ban for repeated failed SSH login attempts -- an active or recent brute-force attempt occurred against this system.

evidence_sources.default_meaning: Clean -- fail2ban has no currently-banned IPs for sshd.

metadata.confidence: verified -- the file-emptiness detection logic is directly confirmed via scanning-lin.py's is_file_empty_or_non_existent() call on this exact path
